ruling.recommended_action: Refund $4.88 to the rider's original payment method for the uninformed surge increase (SURGE-2/SURGE-3); notify the driver that the surge notice must offer a usable free-cancellation option, and log the notice defect on the trip record.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip itself was clean: actual 5.6 km equals the optimal 5.6 km (+0.0 km), well inside RD-1's tolerance, so no route refund arises [F1][F3][RD-1]. The whole disputed $4.88 is the surge change: quote $16.26 at 1×, billed $21.14 at 1.4× from trip start [F6][F7][F5].

The only live element is SURGE-1:notice [F9][SURGE-1]. Reading the quoted text: it names the new multiplier "1.4×" and a revised estimated fare "$22.48" — an estimate that differs from the final charge is still a stated estimate [F5][F9][SURGE-1]. But the third required item — that the rider may cancel without penalty — is contradicted within the notice itself: it says "Free cancellation until 17:13" while the message was sent at 17:14:45, so the option it offers had already expired [F9][SURGE-1]. A cancellation the rider could no longer use is not the free-cancellation element SURGE-1 requires; that element is therefore not_met.

With notice defective, SURGE-2 gives the surge differential: (1.4 − 1.0) × $14.05 = $5.62 [F7][F8][SURGE-3], capped at the $4.88 the fare actually exceeded the quote — $21.14 − $16.26 = $4.88 [F5][F6][F8]. The $1.47 booking fee is not surged and is not refunded [F7][FARE-0]. Both advocates read the notice element the same way, so the only dispute left is quantum, which is $4.88. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider was told she could cancel free is a statement, not a call recording, and does not outweigh the fare log [F13][F9][SURGE-1].

Amount is under $10, so the system decides (TH-1/TH-2, per DISP-001) [F8][TH-1][TH-2]. No route deviation exists, so no RD-6 flag [F1][F3][F15][RD-6]. The chat shows only logistics — "waiting at the taxi stand", "arriving in about 1 min" — with no threat, harassment or dangerous driving anywhere in the chat, the driver's statement or the complaint [F10][F11][F13][SAFE-1].

element_findings.reason: The notice of 17:14:45 states the 1.4× multiplier and a revised estimated fare of $22.48, but its free-cancellation offer reads 'Free cancellation until 17:13' — a deadline already past when the notice was sent — so the option to cancel without penalty was not actually available [F9][SURGE-1]. Any of the three items missing, vague or contradicted within the notice itself makes the notice not_met.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver argues the notice duty was fully performed before departure, but the notice sent at 17:14:45 offers free cancellation only 'until 17:13', so the cancellation element of SURGE-1 was not met on the words of the notice itself [F9][SURGE-1].

The driver argues the rider's riding to completion after being shown the higher fare waives the refund. The chat contains only pickup logistics — 'waiting at the taxi stand', 'arriving in about 1 min' — with no acknowledgement of the new fare, and a post-trip written statement cannot establish informed consent [F10][F11][F12][F13][SURGE-1][SURGE-2].

The rider's added ground that the notice's fare figure is 'materially different' fails: SURGE-1 requires the notice to state a revised estimated fare, and '$22.48' is a stated estimate; an estimate above the final charge of $21.14 does not make the fare element missing [F9][F5][SURGE-1]. The refund rests on the defective cancellation element alone.
Same point as C3 — the notice's $22.48 estimate differs from the billed $21.14 but is still a stated revised estimated fare, so this adds nothing to the outcome [F9][F6][F5][SURGE-1].
The rider's clean profile (account age, rating, no upheld disputes) cannot decide the case: profile facts never decide a case alone, and the notice element turns on the words of F9 [F14][F15][TH-3].
